+# Wang Conjecture 5.3: an Ordinary Semigroup Algebra Counterexample
+
+## Abstract
+
+Wang's Conjecture 5.3 fails for a six-element finite commutative monoid over Q: the ordinary algebraic constant is one and the proposed right side is at least two.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Positive multiples without adjoining zero).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.positiveMultiple`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.positiveMultiple` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Index n denotes the positive multiple (n+1)a. The universal assertion requires only a finite commutative semigroup, with no identity assumption.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The positive cyclic subsemigroup).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.cyclic`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.cyclic` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The carrier consists of positive multiples only. It excludes an artificial zeroth multiple in a nonunital semigroup.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Cyclic idempotent specification).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.IsCyclicIdempotent`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.IsCyclicIdempotent` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The element belongs to the positive cyclic subsemigroup and satisfies e+e=e.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (The actual cyclic idempotent).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.cyclicIdempotent`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.cyclicIdempotent` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A finite positive cyclic subsemigroup has a unique idempotent. Existence reuses Mathlib's compact-semigroup theorem with the discrete topology; uniqueness uses common positive multiples. The selector's fallback is unreachable for every element of a finite commutative semigroup.
+
+**Definition 1.5 (A cyclic group with its own identity).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.CyclicIsGroup`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.CyclicIsGroup` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+An identity and inverses must lie inside the positive cyclic subsemigroup. This property, rather than idempotence alone, controls epsilon.
+
+**Definition 1.6 (The cyclic period).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.period`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.period` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Take the least positive eventual shift of positive multiples. This is the source period, not the index where periodicity begins.
+
+**Definition 1.7 (LCM of the periods).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.semigroupExponent`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.semigroupExponent` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The exponent is the least common multiple of all cyclic periods. The six-label witness has period one at each element and exponent one.
+
+**Definition 1.8 (The source splitting condition).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.Splitting`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.Splitting` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The root set zeta^exp(S)=1 has cardinality exp(S). Extended cardinality retains the distinction between a finite root count and an infinite set.
+
+**Definition 1.9 (Both admissibility branches).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.Admissible`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.Admissible` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Either the splitting condition holds, or K has prime characteristic p and the exponent is a power of p. Branch (i) requires neither algebraic closure nor characteristic zero. Q is used only for the counterexample.
+
+**Definition 1.10 (A factor in the ordinary semigroup algebra).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.factor`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.factor` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Reuse AddMonoidAlgebra K S: coefficients are finitely supported on all of S, and multiplication is the upstream convolution. The factor is the basis vector at s minus a times the basis vector at its cyclic idempotent. Even an absorbing semigroup label remains an independent basis vector.
+
+**Definition 1.11 (Positive products in a possibly nonunital algebra).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.factorProduct`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.factorProduct` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Multiply the ordered factors associatively for every positive length. The empty branch is zero and supplies no positive admissible length; no unit is asserted for an arbitrary nonunital semigroup algebra.
+
+**Definition 1.12 (Every tuple of individually nonzero coefficients).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.GoodSequence`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.GoodSequence` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Quantify over a separate coefficient at each position, requiring it to be nonzero at every position of the finite sequence. Coefficients outside that prefix do not enter the product. Repeated semigroup labels still have independently chosen coefficients.
+
+**Definition 1.13 (The algebraic Davenport constant).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.algebraicD`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.algebraicD` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Take the ENat supremum of all admissible finite lengths. Infinity means unboundedness of finite lengths, without defining an infinite product. Length zero contributes only the bottom of this supremum. In particular, an empty semigroup has constant zero as stipulated by the paper.
+
+**Definition 1.14 (Actual principal ideals).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.Below`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.Below` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Membership means x=a or x=a+c for a genuine semigroup element c. Including a itself does not require an adjoined identity.
+
+**Definition 1.15 (Green H-equivalence).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.Green`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.Green` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Two elements are equivalent exactly when their principal ideals are equal.
+
+**Definition 1.16 (The Green congruence).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.greenCon`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.greenCon` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Equality of principal ideals is an additive congruence in a commutative semigroup; the proof establishes compatibility with addition. Use its upstream AddCon quotient and canonical quotient map directly. For the witness, an exact finite check of principal ideals proves this map injective.
+
+**Definition 1.17 (Sequence sums and existing identities).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.SequenceSum`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.SequenceSum` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A nonempty list sums by the semigroup operation. The empty list sums to a only when a is already a two-sided identity in that semigroup.
+
+**Definition 1.18 (Irreducibility at a specified sum).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.IrreducibleAt`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.IrreducibleAt` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The sequence sums to a and no proper sublist has the same sum. Empty sublists are included. In a commutative semigroup, lists enumerate the unordered sequences and their submultisets without changing sums.
+
+**Definition 1.19 (The relative Davenport constant).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.relativeD`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.relativeD` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Take the ENat supremum of irreducible lengths at the given sum, retaining the source's relative constant rather than a global reducibility threshold.
+
+**Definition 1.20 (The actual H-class).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.HClass`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.HClass` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The class is a subtype of S consisting of elements with the same principal ideal.
+
+**Definition 1.21 (Actual stabilizer translations).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.Gamma`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.Gamma` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The carrier consists of maps H_a to itself realized by c+x for a genuine c in S. Equal maps are identified. Addition is composition, corresponding to addition of realizing elements. No identity is adjoined; the carrier is allowed to be empty.
+
+**Definition 1.22 (The source epsilon).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.epsilon`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.epsilon` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Epsilon is zero exactly for a positive cyclic group, and one otherwise.
+
+**Definition 1.23 (The complete proposed right side).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.rightSide`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.rightSide` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Take the supremum over a in S of epsilon(a) times the relative Davenport constant at the canonical quotient image, plus the algebraic constant of the actual translation semigroup. For finite S this is the finite maximum appearing in the conjecture.
+
+**Definition 1.24 (The complete universal assertion).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.claim`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Quantify over all finite commutative semigroups and fields satisfying either source branch. Assert equality of the two source constants. The finite monoid counterexample is substituted into this full semigroup assertion; the claim imposes no global monoid or sequence-length restriction.
+
+**Definition 1.25 (The six semigroup labels).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.Model`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.Model` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The carrier is {0,1} times {0,1,2}. All six labels remain in the ordinary algebra.
+
+**Definition 1.26 (Union and truncated addition).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.modelAdd`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.modelAdd` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Add by maximum in the first coordinate and min(2,n+m) in the second. The finite commutative monoid laws are checked by Lean's kernel.
+
+**Definition 1.27 (Cyclic idempotents of the witness).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.modelE`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.modelE` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Level zero remains zero; levels one and two have cyclic idempotent level two, with the first coordinate retained.
+
+**Definition 1.28 (The transient term).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.transient`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.transient` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The label (0,1) gives an always-nonzero singleton factor, detected by its coefficient one at this independent basis label.
+
+**Definition 1.29 (The marker term).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.marker`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.marker` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The label (1,0), together with the transient term, forms an irreducible two-term sequence at the target in the canonical quotient.
+
+**Definition 1.30 (The target quotient class).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.target`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S0/Certificates/Algebra/WangConjecture53Refutation.target` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Guoqing Wang (2025). *Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups*. URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18724v1>.
+

+/-- Index n denotes the positive multiple (n+1)a, without adjoining an identity. -/
+def positiveMultiple {S : Type*} [Add S] (a : S) : ℕ → S
+  | 0 => a
+  | n + 1 => positiveMultiple a n + a
+
+/-- The positive cyclic subsemigroup, including no artificial zeroth multiple. -/
+def cyclic {S : Type*} [Add S] (a : S) : Set S := Set.range (positiveMultiple a)
+
+/-- The source's cyclic idempotent specification. -/
+def IsCyclicIdempotent {S : Type*} [Add S] (a e : S) : Prop :=
+  e ∈ cyclic a ∧ e + e = e
+
+/-- Choose the cyclic idempotent; the fallback is irrelevant whenever one exists. -/
+def cyclicIdempotent {S : Type*} [Add S] (a : S) : S := by
+  classical
+  exact if h : ∃ e, IsCyclicIdempotent a e then h.choose else a
+
+/-- Being a group with an identity in the positive cyclic subsemigroup itself. -/
+def CyclicIsGroup {S : Type*} [Add S] (a : S) : Prop :=
+  ∃ e ∈ cyclic a, (∀ x ∈ cyclic a, e + x = x) ∧
+    ∀ x ∈ cyclic a, ∃ y ∈ cyclic a, x + y = e
+
+/-- Least positive eventual shift of the positive multiples: the cyclic period. -/
+def period {S : Type*} [Add S] (a : S) : ℕ :=
+  sInf {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ ∃ k, ∀ m, k ≤ m →
+    positiveMultiple a (m + n) = positiveMultiple a m}
+
+/-- LCM of cyclic periods, rather than cyclic indices or sizes. -/
+def semigroupExponent (S : Type*) [Add S] [Finite S] : ℕ := by
+  letI := Fintype.ofFinite S
+  exact Finset.univ.lcm (period (S := S))
+
+/-- The paper's root-count definition; encard also distinguishes infinite root sets. -/
+def Splitting (S K : Type*) [Add S] [Finite S] [Field K] : Prop :=
+  {z : K | z ^ semigroupExponent S = 1}.encard = semigroupExponent S
+
+/-- Both source admissibility alternatives, with no characteristic restriction in (i). -/
+def Admissible (S K : Type*) [Add S] [Finite S] [Field K] : Prop :=
+  Splitting S K ∨ ∃ p k : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ CharP K p ∧ semigroupExponent S = p ^ k
+
+/-- The ordinary semigroup-algebra factor; every semigroup label is retained. -/
+def factor {S K : Type*} [AddCommSemigroup S] [Field K] (s : S) (a : K) :
+    AddMonoidAlgebra K S :=
+  AddMonoidAlgebra.single s 1 - AddMonoidAlgebra.single (cyclicIdempotent s) a
+
+/-- Positive products do not presume that a general semigroup algebra has a unit.
+The empty branch is unused for positive lengths; zero is included separately in d. -/
+def factorProduct {S K : Type*} [AddCommSemigroup S] [Field K] :
+    List S → (ℕ → K) → AddMonoidAlgebra K S
+  | [], _ => 0
+  | [s], c => factor s (c 0)
+  | s :: t :: l, c => factor s (c 0) * factorProduct (t :: l) (fun i => c (i+1))
+

+def GoodSequence {S K : Type*} [AddCommSemigroup S] [Field K] (l : List S) : Prop :=
+  ∀ c : ℕ → K, (∀ i, i < l.length → c i ≠ 0) → factorProduct l c ≠ 0

+not a finite sequence or an asserted infinite product. Adding zero changes no supremum. -/
+def algebraicD (S K : Type*) [AddCommSemigroup S] [Field K] : ℕ∞ :=
+  ⨆ (l : List S) (_ : GoodSequence (K := K) l), (l.length : ℕ∞)

+  · exact g

+    · exact Or.inr ⟨c, rfl⟩
+    · exact Or.inr ⟨d+c, add_assoc _ _ _⟩

+private theorem green_add_right {S : Type*} [AddCommSemigroup S] {a b : S}

+  have hab : Below a b := (h a).mp (Or.inl rfl)
+  have hba : Below b a := (h b).mpr (Or.inl rfl)

+    rcases hxy with rfl | ⟨d, rfl⟩
+    · exact Or.inl rfl
+    · exact Or.inr ⟨d, by ac_rfl⟩

+  exact ⟨fun hx => below_trans hx (step hab), fun hx => below_trans hx (step hba)⟩

+/-- The actual Green congruence, not a numerical proxy. -/

+  add' := by
+    intro a b c d hab hcd
+    have h₁ := green_add_right hab c
+    have h₂ : Green (b+c) (b+d) := by
+      simpa only [add_comm] using green_add_right hcd b
+    simpa only [add_comm c b, add_comm d b] using

+/-- A sequence sum with the source's empty-sum convention: the empty sequence

+def SequenceSum {S : Type*} [AddSemigroup S] : List S → S → Prop

+/-- Proper subsequences include the empty one. Enumerating unordered sequences

+def IrreducibleAt {S : Type*} [AddSemigroup S] (l : List S) (a : S) : Prop :=
+  SequenceSum l a ∧ ∀ u, u.Sublist l → u.length < l.length → ¬ SequenceSum u a

+  ⨆ (l : List S) (_ : IrreducibleAt l a), (l.length : ℕ∞)

+/-- The H-class as a subtype of the actual carrier. -/

+    rcases g.property with ⟨d, hd⟩

+    AddCommSemigroup (Gamma a) where

+    apply Subtype.ext
+    funext x
+    apply Subtype.ext

+    rcases g.property with ⟨d, hd⟩

+(\Lambda^r-2)h_0\le2h_{2r}.
+$$
+
+On the entire cancellation locus, Theorem 4.2 gives
+
+$$
+2h_{2r}=2t+2^rh_0+\sum_{i=1}^{r-1}2^{r-i}h_i.

+
+Substitution proves (25). For an exact attaining image, Corollary 3.2 supplies $h\in\mathcal K_r$, so the same calculation applies. $\square$

+**Theorem 7.3 (Uniform exclusion of an unbounded positive family).** For every integer $r\ge5$, one has $D_r>1/4$. For every such $r$ and every integer $N\ge2^{r+2}$, set
+
+$$
+h_0=N,\qquad h_1=\cdots=h_{r-1}=t=1,\qquad
+h_{r+j}=2^{j-1}(N+1)\quad(1\le j\le r).
+\tag{28}
+$$
+
+This is a positive cancellation row. Every nonerasing dictionary with this row into every nonempty finite alphabet satisfies
+
+$$
+E(\eta(u))\ge e_r+
+\frac{D_rN-2^r}
+ {\bigl((2^r+1)N+2^r\bigr)(\Lambda^r-1)}
+>e_r.
+\tag{29}
+$$
+
+*Proof.* Put $a=2^r$ and $y=\Lambda^r$. Since $\Lambda=2+1/y$, the binomial inequality gives
+
+$$
+y=\left(2+\frac1y\right)^r\ge a+\frac{ra}{2y}.
+$$
+
+If $y\le a+9/4$, then, since $r\ge5$ and $a\ge32$,
+
+$$
+\frac{ra}{2y}\ge\frac{ra}{2(a+9/4)}
+\ge\frac52\frac{32}{32+9/4}
+=\frac{320}{137}>\frac94.
+$$
+
+This would give $y>a+9/4$, a contradiction. Thus $D_r=y-a-2>1/4$.

+Theorem 4.2 applied to the independent parameters in (28) gives
+
+$$
+t+\sum_{i=0}^{j-1}2^{j-1-i}h_i
+=1+2^{j-1}N+(2^{j-1}-1)=2^{j-1}(N+1).
+$$

+
+$$
+E(\eta(u))\ge2+\frac{N}{(2^r+1)N+2^r}.
+$$
+

+
+$$
+D_rN>\frac{N}{4}\ge2^r.
+$$
+
+The denominator is positive as well. This proves the exclusion for every dictionary with the prescribed lengths, including those with infinite exponent. The family is unbounded since $N$ is arbitrary above the stated threshold. This argument excludes neither all cancellation rows nor any family at $r=3$ or $r=4$. $\square$

+## 8. Length restrictions for the literal prefix class
+
+**Definition 8.1 (Same-morphism literal prefix class).** A pair $(\eta,p)$ belongs to $\mathcal L_r$ if $`\eta:A_r^*\to B^*`$ is an injective nonerasing morphism into a finite alphabet, $p$ is a nonempty palindrome, and for every $i\in A_r$ there is a palindrome $q_i$, possibly empty, such that
+
+$$
+\eta(i)=p q_i,\qquad \eta(i)p=pq_ip
+\text{ has exactly two occurrences of }p,
+$$
+
+at its prefix and suffix. Put $m=|p|\ge1$. An attaining pair additionally satisfies $E(\eta(u))=e_r$. This is the literal representation in Dvořáková–Pelantová, journal Definition 19, [doi:10.37236/14600](https://doi.org/10.37236/14600), arXiv Definition 18. The same $\eta$ acts on the original $u$; no conjugation, replacement by a derived sequence, or change of source is included in this definition.
+
+**Theorem 8.2 (Marker and total-length relaxations).** For every $r\ge3$ and every attaining pair $(\eta,p)\in\mathcal L_r$,
+
+$$
+h_{2r}\ge m(\Lambda^r-1),\qquad
+H\ge(m+1)S_r-2^r.
+\tag{30}
+$$
+
+Equality in the second bound can occur only with the independent parameters
+
+$$
+h_0=m,\qquad h_1=\cdots=h_{r-1}=t=m+1.
+\tag{31}
+$$
+
+For $r=3$ this gives $H\ge28$. Equality $H=28$ forces $m=1$ and the full row
+
+$$
+(h_0,\ldots,h_6)=(1,2,2,2,3,6,12).
+\tag{32}
+$$
+
+These are necessary length conditions; (31) and (32) do not assert the existence of an attaining dictionary.
+
+*Proof.* Write $c=2r$. The letter $c$ occurs in $u$, and $u=\varphi(u)$ contains $cc0$: use the suffix $cc$ of $\varphi(c)=0cc$ and the initial $0$ of the following letter image. Since $\eta(0)$ begins with $p$, the word
+
+$$
+z=\eta(c)\eta(c)p
+$$
+
+is an actual factor of $\eta(u)$. The word $p$ is a prefix of $\eta(c)$, so $|\eta(c)|=h_c$ is a period of $z$. Consequently
+
+$$
+E(\eta(u))\ge2+\frac{m}{h_c}.
+$$
+
+For an attaining pair, (27) now gives the first bound in (30).
+
+Every length $h_i$ is at least $m$. A length equal to $m$ forces $q_i=\varepsilon$ and $\eta(i)=p$. Injectivity permits at most one such $i$. In particular, among the independent parameters $h_0,\ldots,h_{r-1},t$ at most one can equal $m$, and all others are at least $m+1$. Cancellation follows from Corollary 3.2. The exact supplied formula (23) is
+
+$$
+H=(r+1)t+\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}2^{r-i}h_i.
+\tag{33}
+$$
+
+Its coefficient sum is $S_r$. Its unique largest coefficient is $2^r$, at $h_0$, because $2^r>r+1$ for $r\ge3$. Starting with every independent parameter equal to $m+1$, at most one parameter can decrease by one; the greatest possible decrease in (33) is $2^r$. This proves the second inequality in (30). Equality requires the decrease to occur at $h_0$ and requires every other parameter to remain $m+1$, giving (31).
+
+When $r=3$, $S_3=18$, so $H\ge18(m+1)-8$. As $m\ge1$, equality $H=28$ forces $m=1$, $h_0=1$ and $h_1=h_2=t=2$. Formula (19) then gives $h_4=3$, $h_5=6$, $h_6=12$, proving (32).
+
+For comparison, the larger-alphabet attaining supplier in Theorem 4.4 already supplies members of this literal class. Reuse its weighted morphism $\pi_r$ and put $\widehat\eta=\pi_r\circ\varphi$. Its output is the very same supplied word, since $\varphi(u)=u$:
+
+$$
+\widehat\eta(u)=\pi_r(u),\qquad
+E(\widehat\eta(u))=e_r,\qquad
+\#\operatorname{Alph}(\widehat\eta(u))=r+2^r.
+$$
+
+Indeed $\pi_r(0)$ is a single letter $a$ occurring in no other letter image. With $p=a$, the palindromes in the literal representation are
+
+$$
+q_i=\pi_r(i+1)\quad(i<2r),\qquad
+q_{2r}=\pi_r(2r)\pi_r(2r).
+$$
+
+Each $aq_i a$ has exactly two occurrences of $a$. The substitution $\varphi$ is injective, and so is $\pi_r$: its disjoint nonempty image alphabets identify each maximal run of source letters, with the run length determined by the length of its image. Thus $\widehat\eta$ is injective. The richness and exact ordinary exponent are the complete reused conclusions of journal Proposition 14 and Theorem 2, rather than another proof of that construction. Its row is
+
+$$
+\widehat h_i=1+h^*_{i+1}\quad(i<2r),\qquad
+\widehat h_{2r}=1+2h^*_{2r}.
+$$
+
+For $r=3$ it is $(2,2,2,3,5,9,17)$, of total length $40$, on $11$ actual letters. In particular, the length relaxation does not leave all larger-alphabet literal-prefix attainment without a supplied example. $\square$

+## 9. A strengthened boundary on the actual small alphabet
+
+**Theorem 9.1 (The minimal relaxed row forces an ordinary fifth power).** Let $r\ge3$ and $(\eta,p)\in\mathcal L_r$. Suppose that $\eta(u)$ is rich, that its actual alphabet has exactly $r+1$ letters, and that its row is
+
+$$
+h_0=1,\qquad h_i=2\quad(1\le i\le r),\qquad
+h_{r+j}=3\cdot2^{j-1}\quad(1\le j\le r).
+\tag{34}
+$$
+
+Then $\eta(u)$ contains a one-letter fifth power, and hence $E(\eta(u))\ge5$.
+
+*Proof.* Since $1=h_0\ge|p|\ge1$, the marker is a single letter, say $p=a$, and $\eta(0)=a$. For $1\le i\le r$, the literal representation and $h_i=2$ give
+
+$$
+\eta(i)=a b_i
+$$
+
+for a letter $b_i$. The complete-return condition says that $ab_i a$ has exactly two occurrences of $a$, so $b_i\ne a$. Injectivity says that $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ are pairwise distinct. These $r+1$ letters already occur in the output by Definition 7.1. The actual-alphabet hypothesis therefore gives
+
+$$
+\operatorname{Alph}(\eta(u))=\{a,b_1,\ldots,b_r\}.
+\tag{35}
+$$
+
+Set $k=r+2\le2r$. Formula (34) gives $h_k=6$, so $\eta(k)=a q_k$ with $|q_k|=5$. Since $a q_k a$ is a complete return to $a$, the word $q_k$ contains no $a$. By (35), its letters are among $b_1,\ldots,b_r$.
+
+We locate a suitable occurrence in the original source. For $0\le n\le2r$, put $T_n=\varphi^n(0)$. Only the length-two rules are used before constructing $T_{2r}$, and induction on $n$ gives
+
+$$
+|T_n|=2^n,\qquad T_n[j]=\nu_2(j+1)\quad(0\le j<2^n),
+\tag{36}
+$$
+
+where $\nu_2$ is the exponent of $2$ in a positive integer. In the induction step, the even positions become $0$ and the odd positions increase the old letter by one; these are precisely the two corresponding valuation identities. Let $F_{r+1}$ be $T_{r+1}$ with its last letter $r+1$ removed. The last $2^{r+1}$ letters of $T_{r+2}$ are $F_{r+1}(r+2)$ by (36). The word $F_{r+1}$ uses only $0,\ldots,r$, contains every one of those letters, and ends in $0$.
+
+Thus an actual output factor is
+
+$$
+\eta(F_{r+1})a q_k.
+\tag{37}
+$$
+
+In the part $\eta(F_{r+1})a$, each $b_i$ occurs, and every occurrence of a $b_i$ is immediately followed by $a$. This follows from $\eta(0)=a$, $\eta(i)=ab_i$ for $1\le i\le r$, and the final appended $a$.
+
+Let $b$ be the first letter of $q_k$. Suppose that some different letter $d$ occurs in $q_k$, and take its first occurrence there. It is not the first position of $q_k$, and its preceding letter is different from $a$. Take the last occurrence of $d$ in $\eta(F_{r+1})a$. The factor from that occurrence to the chosen first $d$ in $q_k$ contains exactly two $d$'s. It starts with $da$ and ends with $ed$ for a letter $e\ne a$. It cannot be a palindrome, since its second and penultimate letters differ.
+
+But a single letter is a palindrome, and every complete return to a palindromic factor in a rich word is a palindrome. This is exactly Glen–Justin–Widmer–Zamboni, [*Palindromic richness*, arXiv:0801.1656v1, Theorem 2.14 and Remark 2.15](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0801.1656v1), [doi:10.1016/j.ejc.2008.04.006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejc.2008.04.006). That criterion applies to finite and infinite words, without a recurrence or reversal-closure hypothesis. It contradicts the complete return just found. Hence every letter of $q_k$ is $b$, so $q_k=b^5$. This factor has least period one and exponent five, proving the claim. $\square$
+
+**Corollary 9.2 (Length boundary for every nonempty marker).** Let $r\ge3$. Every attaining pair $(\eta,p)\in\mathcal L_r$ whose output is rich on exactly $r+1$ actual letters satisfies
+
+$$
+H\ge2r+3\cdot2^r-2+\gcd(2,r+1).
+\tag{38}
+$$
+
+In particular, for $r=3$ and four actual letters, $H\ge30$. This is a necessary condition in $\mathcal L_r$, with no assertion of feasibility or sharpness at the lower bound.
+
+*Proof.* Write $H_0=2S_r-2^r=2r+3\cdot2^r-2$. If $m\ge2$, Theorem 8.2 gives $H\ge H_0+(m-1)S_r>H_0$. If $m=1$, the same theorem gives $H\ge H_0$, with equality possible only at $h_0=1$, $h_1=\cdots=h_{r-1}=t=2$. The complete supplied family (19) then gives exactly (34). Theorem 9.1 would force $E(\eta(u))\ge5$, whereas (27) and $\Lambda^r>2^r\ge8$ give $e_r<2+1/7<5$. Hence equality is impossible, and $H>H_0$ for every marker length.
+
+Put $g=\gcd(2,r+1)$. Formula (33) shows that $g$ divides $H$. The same formula at the positive cancellation row (34) shows that $g$ divides $H_0$. Therefore the strict integer inequality $H>H_0$ implies $H\ge H_0+g$, proving (38). For $r=3$, $H_0=28$ and $g=2$. The distinction between $m=1$ and $m\ge2$ was only a proof by cases; the corollary imposes no global minimum-marker assumption. $\square$

+## 10. An arithmetic size corollary of the spectral defect
+
+**Corollary 10.1 (Classical norm specialization and near-attainment size).** Let $r\ge3$, let $`\eta:A_r^*\to B^*`$ be any nonerasing morphism into any nonempty finite alphabet, and suppose $hv_\beta\ne0$. With exactly $v_\beta$, $\kappa_r$ and $c_r$ of Definitions 1.3 and Theorem 2.1,
+
+$$
+E(\eta(u))\ge e_r+
+ c_r3^{-(r-1)\kappa_r}H^{-r\kappa_r}
+\ge e_r+\frac{c_r}{27^{r-1}}H^{-3r}.
+\tag{39}
+$$
+
+Consequently, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a noncancelling image satisfying $E(\eta(u))\le e_r+\varepsilon$ must satisfy both
+
+$$
+H\ge3^{-(r-1)/r}\left(\frac{c_r}{\varepsilon}\right)^{1/(r\kappa_r)},
+\qquad
+H\ge\left(\frac{c_r}{27^{r-1}\varepsilon}\right)^{1/(3r)}.
+\tag{40}
+$$
+
+The norm step is classical; (39) is its arithmetic corollary combined with the repo-derived ordinary-factor Theorem 2.1, rather than a new algebraic-norm theorem.
+
+*Proof.* The supplied polynomial $g_r(X)=X^r-\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}X^j$ is the monic minimal polynomial of $\beta$, of degree $r$, as specified in Definition 4.1. Its other complex roots $\zeta_2,\ldots,\zeta_r$ have modulus strictly less than one. The latter fact is supplied both by Appendix P1 of Dvořáková–Pelantová and by the existing $q=r$ statement `dbonacci_complex_root_location` in [DBonacci irreducibility](../../../D5/S0/Tower/DBonacci/Irreducibility.lean); that source also contains its proof-local root-equation argument and the monic integer factor argument used by `dbonacci_irreducible`. The root is the same one fixed by `eq_dbonacciPerronRoot_iff` in [DBonacci Perron root](../../../D5/S0/Tower/DBonacci/PerronRoot.lean). No rescaling of the eigenvector or replacement of the degree is made here.
+
+Define the integer polynomial
+
+$$
+P_h(X)=(X-2)\sum_{i=0}^{2r-1}h_iX^{2r-1-i}+h_{2r},
+$$
+
+so that $\alpha=P_h(\beta)=hv_\beta$. Because $\beta$ is an algebraic integer, $\alpha$ is an algebraic integer in $K=\mathbb Q(\beta)$. The classical norm formulas give
+
+$$
+N_{K/\mathbb Q}(\alpha)
+=P_h(\beta)\prod_{j=2}^{r}P_h(\zeta_j)\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}.
+\tag{41}
+$$
+
+Here the product is over all $r$ embeddings of $K$, even if $\alpha$ generates a proper subfield. These are the standard integrality and conjugate-product norm statements; see J. S. Milne, [*Algebraic Number Theory*, version 3.08, Theorem 2.1, Corollaries 2.20–2.21 and Aside 2.22](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf).
+
+For $j\ge2$, $|\zeta_j|<1$ and $|\zeta_j-2|<3$, whence
+
+$$
+|P_h(\zeta_j)|
+\le |\zeta_j-2|\sum_{i=0}^{2r-1}h_i|\zeta_j|^{2r-1-i}+h_{2r}
+\le3H.
+$$
+
+Taking absolute values in (41), using its nonzero integer value, gives
+
+$$
+1\le|\alpha|(3H)^{r-1},\qquad
+\rho=\frac{|\alpha|}{H}\ge3^{-(r-1)}H^{-r}.
+\tag{42}
+$$
+
+The last lower bound lies in $(0,1]$, since $H\ge1$. Thus
+
+$$
+\min(1,\rho)\ge3^{-(r-1)}H^{-r}.
+$$
+
+Applying Theorem 2.1 proves the first inequality in (39). Its proof already supplies $0<\kappa_r<3$. Since $3^{r-1}H^r\ge1$, raising its reciprocal to $\kappa_r$ gives a value at least its third power, proving the second inequality. Combining each of these positive excess bounds with $E(\eta(u))-e_r\le\varepsilon$ and taking the respective positive roots proves (40).
+
+If $hv_\beta=0$, the integer norm in (41) is zero and the lower bound (42) does not follow. Thus this corollary gives no positive gap on cancellation and no existence of approaching images. $\square$

+## 11. Separate mathematical targets and representation boundaries
+
+**Definition 11.1 (Exact, approaching and unrestricted targets).** For each $r\ge3$, the exact original-source small-alphabet question asks for a nonerasing morphism $\eta$ for which
+
+$$
+\#\operatorname{Alph}(\eta(u_{2r+1}))=r+1,\qquad
+\eta(u_{2r+1})\text{ is rich},\qquad
+E(\eta(u_{2r+1}))=e_r,
+$$
+
+allowing every positive length row and arbitrary morphisms. The distinct approaching question asks for a family with the same actual alphabet size and richness whose ordinary exponents tend to $e_r$. The unrestricted threshold target remains Definition 3.3:
+
+$$
+RT(\mathcal C_d)=E^*(u_{2d-1})\quad(d\ge2),
+$$
+
+where $\mathcal C_d$ contains all infinite rich words on $d$ actual letters, without a recurrence or morphic restriction. Its lower inequality quantifies over every word in that class. The cone, the excluded family and (38) supply necessary restrictions, leaving these existence and unrestricted lower-bound obligations unresolved here, already for the exact original $u_7$ question on four letters. In particular, (38) is not an impossibility assertion for arbitrary morphisms or a construction at $H=30$.
+
+The representation in Definition 8.1 is narrower than the complete-return formulation in Balková–Pelantová–Starosta, [*Infinite words with finite defect*, arXiv:1009.5105v1, Definition 5.1, Proposition 5.4 and Theorem 5.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1009.5105v1), [doi:10.1016/j.aam.2010.11.006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aam.2010.11.006). That formulation allows a return word shorter than its marker and uses conjugation and derived words. A literal factorization $\eta(i)=p q_i$ for the same morphism on the same $u$ is an additional condition. Neither the derived-word representation nor conjugacy alone supplies that condition while preserving this length row. The marker and length conclusions (30) and (38) are restricted to Definition 8.1; they impose no condition on the broader overlapping-return class or on arbitrary rich morphisms without such a bridge.
+
+For the source/exponent distinction, Dvořáková–Klouda–Pelantová, [*The asymptotic repetition threshold of sequences rich in palindromes*, arXiv:2409.06849v1, Theorems 24–25 and Corollary 29](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.06849v1), [doi:10.1016/j.ejc.2025.104124](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejc.2025.104124), supplies a rich binary projection $i\mapsto ab^i$ preserving the asymptotic exponent. This is an asymptotic supplier, not an ordinary-exponent upper bound. Currie–Mol–Peltomäki, [*The repetition threshold for ternary rich words*, EJC 32(2), P2.55, Theorems 1.1–1.2](https://doi.org/10.37236/13499), supplies the ternary ordinary threshold and its transducer construction. Dvořáková–Pelantová, [*Symmetries of rich sequences with minimum critical exponent*, arXiv:2501.15135v1, Proposition 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.15135v1), supplies its original-source morphic representation on $u_5$. These are exact supplied results in their respective ranges, rather than solutions of the original $u_{2r+1}$ problem for $r\ge3$. A finite rich word, including a long word with a controlled exponent, is also distinct from the infinite-word existence required in Definition 3.3.
